title: Read any Japanese label with confidence.
description: Pork, lard, sake, and gelatin hide behind a few recurring kanji. Search them here, learn how to read the ingredients box, and find halal food near you.

hero.disclaimer: This guide is maintained by the congregation and is not a certification. When unsure, ask the maker or choose certified products.

labels.title: How to read a Japanese food label
labels.description: Japanese labels follow a fixed layout. Find these headings first, then scan the ingredients line for the kanji above.

0.meaning: Components or nutrition. Usually a table of calories, protein, fat, and salt.

1.meaning: Ingredients list, ordered from the largest amount. This is the line to read carefully.

2.meaning: Allergen notice. Items in parentheses such as 一部に豚肉を含む reveal pork even when it is not obvious.

3.meaning: Derived from pork. Often written after gelatin or emulsifier.

4.meaning: Gelatin. Haram unless the label says fish (魚) or plant-based (植物性).

5.meaning: Emulsifier. Doubtful; soy-derived (大豆由来) is fine.

6.meaning: Shortening. Doubtful; vegetable only (植物油脂) is fine.

7.meaning: Alcohol added as a preservative, common in miso, soy sauce, and pickles.

labels.tip: Allergen notices list 豚肉 when pork is present in any amount. Reading that one line catches most hidden pork.
